title: GAO: 17 of 22 major agencies had not fully addressed federal guidance in zero trust plans
date_note: GAO's product page states the report was published and publicly released on 18 November 2026.
summary: GAO report GAO-27-108661, released 18 November 2026, says that as of August 2026 five of 22 agencies had addressed OMB or NIST guidance in their zero trust architecture planning, while 17 agencies had not fully done so. GAO is making 40 recommendations to 17 agencies; thirteen agreed. Fox News reports GAO warned the agencies would be at increased risk of cyberattacks.
plain: A US government watchdog found that 17 of 22 major agencies had not fully followed federal guidance in their plans for a security model called zero trust, and made 40 recommendations.
exec: GAO says 17 agencies had not fully addressed federal zero trust guidance and is making 40 recommendations to them.
action: GAO recommends that agencies document zero trust maturity levels, update implementation plans to cover NIST migration steps, and document roles and the implementation process.

evidence.quote: However, 17 agencies had not fully done so.
GAO is making a total of 40 recommendations to 17 agencies to address selected guidance.
Thirteen agencies agreed with the recommendations, and several described planned actions to implement them.
17 of 22 major civilian agencies failed to fully address key cybersecurity planning guidance

validation.note: GAO's product page and its online report text read, plus Fox News; the increased-risk warning is GAO's. The PDF itself was not opened.

key_findings: Almost all of the civilian agencies reviewed had zero trust architecture plans, but as of August 2026 only five had fully addressed the selected OMB and NIST guidance; 17 had not.
The most common OMB gap was documenting zero trust maturity levels for high-value assets and high-impact systems; USDA, Commerce and SBA did not do it at all.
HHS lacked an enterprise-wide plan covering all its systems, and NASA's plan covered only one of its three enterprise environments.
Against NIST guidance, gaps appeared in identifying non-person actors and assets, expanding the architecture, defining project roles and describing the implementation process.
Agencies cited limited staffing and funding, staff attrition and shutdowns; GAO warns this raises the risk of cyberattacks.
recommendations: Document zero trust maturity levels for high-value assets and high-impact systems using CISA's maturity model.
Update zero trust implementation plans to cover NIST migration steps such as identifying actors and assets and expanding the architecture.
Document roles, responsibilities and the implementation process for zero trust efforts.
Create or complete an enterprise-wide zero trust plan (GAO asks this of HHS).

review.note: Compared 5 of 22/17, 40 recommendations, 13 agreed, date and risk wording against GAO page
